sound: small yu, which joins to the preceding sign and makes one mora with it
components: a small ゆ-shaped left stem and broad loop
strokeOrder: descend through the left stem, turn up and right across the high shoulder, then continue clockwise around the broad loop and curve left to the inner finish
lift, begin high above the loop, descend through its center, and curve down and left to the finish
strokeOrderNote: Sirgazil's 30-frame ゆ animation supplies the two-run order; Unicode names U+3085 HIRAGANA LETTER SMALL YU, so the same movement is fitted to its smaller bundled glyph, exactly as U+3063 small tsu is fitted from つ.

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sirgazil, Hiragana ゆ stroke order animation.gif, hiragana ゆ, 30 frames, 3.0 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 1 October 2009); the Unicode Standard names U+3085 HIRAGANA LETTER SMALL YU, alias small yu
strokeOrderSource.variation: The CC0 animation draws full-size ゆ in two pen-down runs with one lift: the left stem, high shoulder and clockwise loop first, then a restart above the loop descending through its center. Unicode separately identifies U+3085 as small yu. This learner path therefore preserves the source's two-run movement while scaling and fitting it to the bundled Noto Sans JP small ゅ outline; the cited animation demonstrates ゆ rather than a separately animated ゅ, so the size adaptation is explicit rather than presented as independent handwriting evidence.

notes: A yōon sign: it does not take a beat of its own but fuses with the sign before it, so じ + ゅ is one mora ju, as in じゅう, ten. Contrast っ, which is a beat of closure rather than a fusion.
